title: A hex dump
description:
Read one line of text and show its UTF-8 bytes as a hex dump, **8 bytes per row**:

```
Text? Hello, world!
0000  48 65 6C 6C 6F 2C 20 77  Hello, w
0008  6F 72 6C 64 21           orld!
```

- The offset is 4 upper-case hex digits.
- Then two spaces, then each byte as two upper-case hex digits followed by a space; a short last row is padded with spaces so the text column lines up (every row's bytes take 8 × 3 characters).
- Then one more space and the bytes as text: printable ASCII (32 to 126) as itself, anything else as `.`.

`text.encode("utf-8")` gives the bytes; `data[i:i + 8]` is up to 8 of them starting at `i`; `f"{n:04X}"` and `f"{b:02X}"` format hex.

solution.main.py:
text = input("Text? ")
data = text.encode("utf-8")
for offset in range(0, len(data), 8):
    row = data[offset:offset + 8]
    hex_part = "".join(f"{b:02X} " for b in row).ljust(8 * 3)
    text_part = "".join(chr(b) if 32 <= b <= 126 else "." for b in row)
    print(f"{offset:04X}  {hex_part} {text_part}")
